system_name: Louisiana Educator Advancement and Development System (LEADS)
key_objectives: Use research-based teaching and leadership standards that provide clear descriptions of practice across a range of indicators.
Provide high-quality feedback to teachers and leaders that is actionable, detailed, and timely.
Support the continuous improvement of teaching and learning using materials teachers use every day in classrooms.
Offer opportunities for teamwork and collaboration that help educators to develop their practice.
Provide differentiated follow-up coaching and support based on refinement areas.
Enable educators to reflect on their practice and share their views as part of the evaluation process.

observation_requirements.teachers_3_plus_years: One unannounced observation. If score < 3.5, second announced observation required. If average of first two < 2.5, third unannounced observation required.

rubric_structure.description: Comprehensive focus on four key domains: Instruction, Planning, Environment, and Professionalism. Each domain is broken down into indicators and descriptors. Performance definitions are provided at levels 5 (Exemplary), 3 (Proficient), and 1 (Unsatisfactory). Observers can score performance at levels 2 or 4 based on evidence and professional judgment.

indicators.overview: Foundation for all other indicators. Teacher and students must understand the rigor of the standard and what students should know/do. Requires planning standards-aligned lessons with clear objectives.
indicators.content_connections: Begin with clear identification of learning objective aligned to state standards and adopted curriculum (HQIM). Standards and objectives align with HQIM scope and sequence.
student_centered_evidence: Students turn objective into essential question.
Students set personal learning goals based on objective.
Students make connections to previous lessons/experiences.
Students deconstruct objective for mastery criteria.
Students return to objective to analyze understanding.
Students assess work against mastery criteria.
Students articulate and explain lesson to peers.

key_terms.Communicated: Learning objectives and standards written so students understand and can articulate what they are learning.
key_terms.Connected: Learning objectives are part of a continuum aligned to standards and curriculum.
key_terms.Expectations: Intentional use of learning targets and pathway to mastery.
key_terms.Mastery: Demonstration by students internalizing and meeting the lesson objective.
key_terms.Student Work: Activities, assignments, products aligning to objectives, demonstrating progress.
key_terms.Sub-Objectives: Prerequisite skills needed for learning target.
key_terms.Referenced: Teacher makes connections between learning objective and lesson activities.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: All learning objectives and state content standards*, and their connection to student work expectations, are explicitly communicated and understood by students.
Objectives and expectations are aligned to the depth and rigor of the state standards; lesson content is aligned to the objectives of the high-quality instructional materials.
Sub-objectives/Prerequisite skills are aligned and logically sequenced to the lesson’s major objective.
Students make connections between learning objectives and (a) what they have previously learned, (b) know from life experiences, and/or (c) knowledge of other disciplines.
Expectations for each student’s performance are clear, demanding, and high, and student work is aligned to state content standards and learning objectives.
Students are able to articulate what they are learning and why and explain those to their peers.
Learning objectives are displayed and referenced throughout the lesson with explanations.
Student work shows evidence that each student is progressing or demonstrating mastery of the objective(s).

descriptor_details.descriptor: All learning objectives and state content standards... explicitly communicated...
descriptor_details.explanation: Objectives must be clearly written (observable verb, clear outcome, measurable criteria). Teacher ensures student understanding through explicit communication, referencing, discussion, and reflection. Vocabulary explicitly taught.
possible_evidence: Student personal goals related to objective

descriptor_details.descriptor: Objectives and expectations are aligned to the depth and rigor...
descriptor_details.explanation: Planning and implementation must ensure academic access for all students at the standard's depth and rigor. Includes clear expectations for procedures and behavior, often using models.
possible_evidence: Lesson objective aligned to standard rigor

descriptor_details.descriptor: Sub-objectives/Prerequisite skills are aligned...
descriptor_details.explanation: Instructional scaffolds via planned sub-objectives ensure pathway to mastery. Reasons: review prior learning, teach new sub-skill, teach supporting process.
possible_evidence: Lesson includes review of prior skills

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students make connections between learning objective(s)...
descriptor_details.explanation: Connect new learning to prior learning and real-life impacts. Supported by curriculum guides and brain science (repeated practice). Relates to Teacher Knowledge of Students (relevancy, interests, culture).
possible_evidence: Teacher explicitly links to prior lessons/units
Activities connect learning to student experiences or other subjects

descriptor_details.descriptor: Expectations for each student’s performance are clear...
descriptor_details.explanation: Demanding, high-quality expectations for all students. Requires diagnostics to determine needs. Measurement criteria must be clear. Includes procedural/behavioral expectations. Models (visuals, demos, rubrics, steps) are crucial. Group work expectations defined.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students are able to articulate what they are learning...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students internalize and can explain learning expectations and purpose to peers. Requires clear communication of expectations for individual/group work, procedures, noise level etc.
possible_evidence: Students answer 'What are you learning and why?'

descriptor_details.descriptor: Learning objectives are displayed and referenced...
descriptor_details.explanation: Displaying objectives connects activities to goals. Must be visible, referenced, and understood. Referencing relates lesson to 'big picture', prior/future learning. Use student-friendly language, visuals, symbols.
possible_evidence: Visual formats (maps, webs) used for objectives

descriptor_details.descriptor: Student work shows evidence that each student is progressing...
descriptor_details.explanation: Focus on evidence of learning aligned with expectations. Student work serves as formative assessment throughout the lesson. Used to check mastery and modify future plans.
possible_evidence: Analysis of student work showing mastery/progress (e.g., % meeting criteria)

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Learning objectives and state content standards* are communicated.
Objectives and expectations are aligned to the depth and rigor of the state standards; lesson content is aligned to the objectives of the high-quality instructional materials.
Sub-objective/Prerequisite skills are aligned to the lesson’s major objective.
Learning objectives are connected to what students have previously learned.
Expectations for student performance are clear.
Learning objectives are displayed.
There is evidence that students are progressing or demonstrating mastery of the objective(s).

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Some learning objectives and state content standards* are communicated.
Sub-objectives/Prerequisite skills are inconsistently aligned to the lesson’s major objective.
Learning objectives are rarely connected to what students have previously learned.
Expectations for student performance are vague.
Learning objectives are displayed.
There is little evidence that students are progressing or demonstrating mastery of the objective(s).

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you decide on the standards/objectives you will teach?
How do you ensure the rigor of the learning is aligned to the rigor of the standard?
How do you identify the sub-objectives/pre-requisite skills for a lesson?
How will you build background knowledge for students who need it to ensure they have access to the lesson’s objective?
How do you decide on the method you will use to communicate the standards/objectives to students?
How will you know if students understand the standards/objectives?
How can students have opportunities to set goals and monitor their progress toward the lesson objective?
How will students utilize and reference the visual of the standards/objectives during a lesson?
How will the expectations for student performance be communicated to students?
How will you know students understand the expectations for student performance?
How will students make connections between previous learning and life experiences and the lesson ‘s objective?
How will you obtain evidence that most or all students have demonstrated mastery of the objective? What will this evidence look like?
How will students know they have mastered the lesson’s objective?

indicators.overview: Focuses on teacher's ability to organize and present content to motivate students. Requires in-depth knowledge of students and content/HQIM. Blending knowledge of content/curriculum with student learning needs creates rigorous, motivating experiences.
indicators.content_connections: Articulates teacher's ability to bring HQIM to life. Curriculum resources provide launching pad for motivating, engaging lessons supporting intellectual development and access.
student_centered_evidence: Students can articulate the purpose of the lesson and why it is important to them.
Students grapple with concepts and explore the lesson materials.
Students are motivated to accomplish the task and persevere through the assigned student work.
Students ask questions, challenge ideas, and inquire about topics.
Students thoughtfully consider various perspectives/alternatives/solutions, analyzing the pros and cons of each, before selecting one to support.
Students initiate their own pursuit of answers and solutions.
Students continue discussion about the learning outside of the designated time for the lesson.

key_terms.Curiosity: A strong desire to learn or know something.
key_terms.Engaging: Explicit attention, curiosity, interest, or passion students demonstrate when learning.
key_terms.Exploration: Providing students with active learning experiences (engaging visuals, hands-on, intellectually captivating content).
key_terms.Inquiry: Instruction that triggers and activates a student’s curiosity.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: The teacher consistently organizes the content, including high-quality curriculum resources, so that it is personally meaningful, relevant, and intellectually engaging to students.
The teacher consistently develops learning experiences where inquiry, curiosity, and exploration are valued.
Students are consistently engaged in their own learning, and the teacher reinforces students’ initiative to learn more.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher consistently organizes the content... personally meaningful, relevant, and intellectually engaging...
descriptor_details.explanation: Content needs communicated purpose. Students need to understand why it's essential and how it impacts their lives. Requires planning rigorous/relevant HQIM with strategies for questioning, conversing, deep learning connections.
possible_evidence: Lesson connects to current events/student lives

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher consistently develops learning experiences where inquiry, curiosity, and exploration are valued.
descriptor_details.explanation: Provide opportunities for students to generate questions, research, explore answers. Increases motivation as learning becomes more student-directed.
possible_evidence: Students develop their own research questions

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students are consistently engaged... teacher reinforces students’ initiative...
descriptor_details.explanation: Reflects teacher support for student ownership. Reinforce initiative by encouraging exploration, research, self-selected topics. Academic feedback acknowledging questions/extending learning reinforces initiative. Safe environment for risk-taking.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: The teacher organizes the content, including high-quality curriculum resources, so that it is personally meaningful and relevant to students.
The teacher develops learning experiences where inquiry, curiosity, and exploration are valued.
The teacher regularly reinforces and rewards effort.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The teacher sometimes organizes the content, including high-quality curriculum resources, so that it is personally meaningful and relevant to students.
The teacher seldom develops learning experiences where inquiry, curiosity, and exploration are valued.
The teacher rarely reinforces and rewards effort.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you organize the content of a lesson so that it is personally meaningful, relevant, and intellectually engaging to students?
How will you ensure the lesson is both rigorous and motivating for all students?
How do you leverage high-quality curriculum and materials to develop learning experiences that provide opportunities for students to ask questions and explore?
Why is it important for students to have opportunities to develop their own questions and explore answers for those questions?
How will students be engaged in learning throughout the lesson and take initiative for their own learning?

indicators.overview: Connects to method(s) of teaching content. Addresses visuals, concise communication, logical sequencing. Visuals (examples, illustrations, analogies, labels) essential for new/rigorous concepts. Use effectively and appropriately.
indicators.content_connections: Requires deep understanding of standards and HQIM. Teacher must be informed on skills to make decisions on how to best share, inform, scaffold, present content.
student_centered_evidence: Students reference visuals and examples presented during application.
Students utilize example/exemplar to create success criteria, products, or assess work.
Students record notes on steps during teacher model.
Students have opportunity to reflect orally or in writing.
Students reference previous anchor charts/visuals and use learned strategies.

key_terms.Internal Summaries: Periodic pause during lesson to review steps toward mastery objective. Reinforces/clarifies essential ideas.
key_terms.Modeling: Instructional strategy where teacher demonstrates new concept, thinking, or learning approach; students learn by observing/hearing.
key_terms.Performance Expectations: Requirements of student (expected results, behavior, criteria, actions) to meet objective/target (measurement/success criteria).
key_terms.Essential Information: Information extremely important or necessary for lesson, situation, activity, or mastery.
key_terms.Logical Sequencing and Segmenting: Effective sequence provides relationship pattern for activities. Proper sequencing avoids inconsistencies.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: visuals, including student work exemplars, that establish the purpose of the lesson, preview the organization of the lesson, and include internal summaries of the lesson;
examples, illustrations, analogies, and labels for new concepts and ideas;
modeling by the teacher or student that demonstrates accurate understanding of the content and meets performance expectations;
criteria that clarifies how students can be successful;
concise communication;
logical sequencing and segmenting;
all essential information; and
no irrelevant, confusing, or nonessential information.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Visuals, including student work exemplars...
descriptor_details.explanation: Effective use of visuals to connect prior learning, clarify concepts, provide direction. Two applications: assist learning process, organize information. Internal summaries (mini-reviews) can be visual or oral.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Examples, illustrations, analogies, and labels...
descriptor_details.explanation: Clarifying techniques to simplify/organize new info. Leverage HQIM guidance. Examples (for concepts), Illustrations (diagrams, images), Analogies (comparisons), Labels (clarify info, vocabulary).
possible_evidence: Teacher uses specific examples for concepts

descriptor_details.descriptor: Modeling by the teacher or student...
descriptor_details.explanation: Ability to model new info and expectations is crucial. Requires knowing outcome, identifying critical elements (success criteria), defining steps, providing exemplars. Students can acquire skills to provide coherent models.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Criteria that clarifies how students can be successful;
descriptor_details.explanation: Concrete list of performance expectations (process success criteria) for students to obtain mastery. Helps with focus during rigorous learning/heavy cognitive load. Product success criteria clarify final output.
possible_evidence: Explicit list of steps/actions for task (process criteria)
Rubric or checklist for final product (product criteria)

descriptor_details.descriptor: Concise communication; Logical sequencing and segmenting; All essential information; No irrelevant...
descriptor_details.explanation: Relates to teacher knowledge of content/HQIM and ability to explain logically. Requires clear objective definition and maintaining focus. Sequencing relates to sub-objectives/prerequisites. Segmenting includes pacing and structuring, breaking down components.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: visuals that establish the purpose of the lesson, preview the organization of the lesson, and include internal summaries of the lesson;
examples, illustrations, analogies, and labels for new concepts and ideas;
modeling by the teacher to demonstrate his or her performance expectations;
criteria that clarifies how students can be successful;
concise communication;
logical sequencing and segmenting;
all essential information; and
no irrelevant, confusing, or nonessential information.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: visuals that establish the purpose of the lesson, preview the organization of the lesson, and include internal summaries of the lesson;
examples, illustrations, analogies, and labels for new concepts and ideas;
modeling by the teacher to demonstrate his or her performance expectations;
criteria that clarifies how students can be successful;
concise communication;
logical sequencing and segmenting;
all essential information; and
no irrelevant, confusing, or nonessential information.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you decide on the types of visuals you will use during a lesson?
How will these visuals support student learning?
How do you expect students will use the visuals to support their learning?
What examples, illustrations, analogies, or labels for new concepts will be used in the lesson? How will these support student learning?
How do you expect that students will utilize the examples, illustrations, analogies, or labels to support their learning?
Why is it important for the teacher and student to model performance expectations? How will the performance expectations be modeled in this lesson?
How does the model of performance expectations provide access to content for all learners?
How will students clearly know the criteria for their assignments and for what they are to learn?
When planning a lesson, how do you decide on the sequencing of the instruction within the lesson?
When planning a lesson, how do you decide on the manner in which the different elements of the lesson will be segmented?
How do you maintain focus on the learning objectives during a lesson?
When planning content that is especially rigorous, how does strategic presentation of that content impact students’ learning?

indicators.overview: Blends time and form. Addresses effective segmentation for sufficient time allocation. Connects to 'logical sequencing and segmenting' under PIC. Requires thoughtful structure/pacing for motivation and engagement.
indicators.content_connections: Leverage HQIM guidance for aligned, coherent structures organized for student needs, including reflection time. Align structure with adopted curriculum (anticipatory sets, direct instruction, guiding questions, small groups, checks for understanding).
student_centered_evidence: Students set goals and reflect on learning orally or in writing.
Students finishing early engage in additional HQIM activities.
Students purposefully move between activities.
Students are aware of time guidelines, monitor/adjust pacing.
Students can explain purpose of routines/transitions.

key_terms.Promptly: Students engaged in meaningful activity connected to objective at beginning of period.
key_terms.Coherent: Logical connection from one segment to next with clear progression.
key_terms.Brisk: Efficient and effective use of instructional time.
key_terms.Learning Rates: Amount of time student may take to complete task.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: The lesson starts promptly.
The lesson’s structure is coherent, based on the content, and organized to meet students’ needs, with time for reflection to ensure student understanding.
Pacing is brisk, adjusted for rigor of content and individual student learning expectations.
Students’ individual needs are attended to, and pacing provides many opportunities for individual students who progress at different learning rates.
Students understand and engage in classroom routines and transitions to ensure efficient use of time.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The lesson starts promptly.
descriptor_details.explanation: Students engaged for entirety of lesson. Begin promptly to maximize time. Plan/implement opening activities that jump start thinking aligned to objective.
possible_evidence: Students immediately engage in opening task

descriptor_details.descriptor: The lesson’s structure is coherent...
descriptor_details.explanation: Structure planned for coherence and alignment with content/HQIM guidance. Arrange beginning/middle/end to meet student needs and allow reflection time.
possible_evidence: Lesson plan follows HQIM structure (e.g., beginning/middle/end)

descriptor_details.descriptor: Pacing is brisk, adjusted for the rigor...
descriptor_details.explanation: 'Brisk' means efficient use of time (per curriculum recs), not speed. Appropriate time devoted to each element based on rigor. Flow maintained, no wasted time. Teacher facilitates movement toward challenging work.
possible_evidence: Lesson progresses smoothly without significant downtime
Teacher adjusts pacing based on student understanding/needs

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students’ individual needs are attended to...
descriptor_details.explanation: Challenge is attending to individual needs while allowing time for all varying learners to complete tasks. Requires knowing student needs/difficulties and planning accordingly.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students understand and engage in classroom routines...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students can explain routines and carry out with minimal redirection. Checks for understanding critical for routines. Ensures efficient time use.
possible_evidence: Students can explain group work routines
Minimal time lost during transitions/material distribution

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: The lesson starts promptly.
The lesson’s structure is coherent, based on the content, and has a beginning, middle, and end, with time for reflection to ensure student understanding.
Pacing is appropriate and sometimes provides opportunities for students who progress at different learning rates.
Routines for distributing materials are efficient.
Little instructional time is lost during transitions.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The lesson does not start promptly.
The lesson has a structure, but may be missing key components of the content, or it may not include reflection or introductory elements.
Pacing rarely provides opportunities for students who progress at different learning rates.
Routines for distributing materials are inefficient.
Considerable time is lost during transitions.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you decide on how you will segment different parts of a lesson? How will these segments ensure student progress toward mastery of the lesson objective(s)?
How do you plan for effective closure and reflection within a lesson? How will students reflect on their progress toward mastering the objective?
How will the lesson be adjusted to allow for depth and rigor of content and individual student expectations?
How do you plan to pace the lesson to provide opportunities for students who progress at different rates?
How do you ensure that instructional time is used efficiently throughout a lesson so that all students remain actively engaged in learning?
How does the structure of the lesson promote student ownership?
How does the structure and pacing of the lesson ensure that students maintain motivation while continuously engaging with rigorous content?

indicators.overview: Addresses variety and appropriateness of activities/materials. Requires positive/supportive environment (Environment domain). After establishing expectations, leverage curriculum-driven activities/materials. Purposeful activities/materials support objectives and challenge students.
indicators.content_connections: Curriculum provides the 'what', activities/materials are 'how'. Plan activities aligned to standard's rigor, leverage materials to move students to mastery. Often part of formative assessment.
student_centered_evidence: Students share how activity connects to objective.
Students explain how activities build understanding.
Students use HQ activities/materials to construct understanding.
Students take initiative/persevere in challenging activities.
Students cognitively engaged in tasks facilitating thinking/interaction.
Students ask questions/generate ideas during activities.
Students learn with/from others in collaborative groups.
Students complete work meeting expectations/mastery criteria.
Students reflect on progress toward mastery.

key_terms.Activities: Actions students/teachers take, designed/deployed by teacher for learning.
key_terms.Materials: Supplies/resources from HQIM used for practical activities.
key_terms.Supplementary Resources: Materials, ideas, examples, textbooks, videos to enhance/differentiate when not in HQIM.
key_terms.Support Standards-Based Challenge: Activities/materials provide succinct path to mastery aligned with standards, challenging students.
key_terms.Relevant: Student-centered term: evoke curiosity/suspense, relevant to lives.
key_terms.Interaction: Student-centered term: opportunities for student-to-student interaction.
key_terms.Self-Direction: Student-centered term: provide choices, demand self-direction/monitoring.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Content: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; and are relevant to students’ lives.

Student-centered: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; and provide students with choices when appropriate and aligned to the learning objectives.

Multiple materials: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

In addition, sometimes activities are game-like, involve simulations, require creating products, and demand self-direction, and students are continuously self-monitoring as appropriate to enhance learning.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Content: support the lesson objectives; are challenging...
descriptor_details.explanation: Critical that activities/materials support content/HQIM and create meaningful learning. Must be thoughtfully identified from curriculum to support objective. Purposeful use required. Challenging for all, not just a few. Relates to TKS and Thinking indicators.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Student-centered: sustain students’ attention...
descriptor_details.explanation: Effectively curated activities/materials bring content to life, sustain attention, evoke curiosity/suspense. Provide opportunities for interaction, peer learning, meaningful choices.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Multiple materials: incorporate additional standards-based resources...
descriptor_details.explanation: Use of additional materials/tools (visuals, tech, manipulatives, external resources) when appropriate and not available in HQIM/curriculum.
possible_evidence: Use of supplementary texts, videos, websites
Guest speakers or virtual field trips

descriptor_details.descriptor: In addition, sometimes activities are game-like...
descriptor_details.explanation: Prompts planning/implementing rigorous activities (aligned to standards/curriculum) that feel game-like, involve simulations, creation, self-direction, self-monitoring.
possible_evidence: Students monitor own progress on long-term tasks

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Content: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; and are relevant to students’ lives.

Student-centered: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; and provide students with choices when appropriate and aligned to the learning objectives.

Multiple materials: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Content: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; or are relevant to students’ lives.
Student-centered: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; or provide students with choices.

Multiple materials: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

suggested_coaching_questions: How can you be sure the identified/planned activities and materials support the learning and guide students directly toward mastery of the lesson objective? How do you leverage the high-quality curriculum and materials to plan for activities within a lesson?
How will you provide challenging activities and materials for all students in your class?
How will you maintain all students’ attention during the lesson?
How will you allow for meaningful student-to-student interaction so that students can learn with and from one another?
What activities and which materials will best set the conditions to evoke student curiosity and suspense?
How will you provide students with choice that is appropriate and aligned to the lesson objective?
How will students create and self-monitor their own learning?
How will you allow for authentic reflection at the close of the learning experience?

indicators.overview: Skill to deepen understanding/ownership. Rubric provides framework for question types and response leading. Align questions to standards/HQIM, increase rigor/ownership. Content-related (purposeful alignment) and procedural-related (engagement processes) descriptors.
indicators.content_connections: HQIM include questions aligned to standards. Review for alignment/rigor. Use as launch for discussion/inquiry. Identify additional questions for background knowledge/scaffolding. Plan sequence of rigorous, curriculum-derived questions.
student_centered_evidence: Students respond to variety of questions.
Students actively discuss responses (partners, small/whole group).
Students generate individual responses before sharing.
Students are inquisitive, generate questions to deepen thinking.
Students use each other’s questions to spark more.
Students take initiative to ask clarifying questions/push thinking.
Students question own work via reflection.

key_terms.Question Types: Different types teacher should plan (Knowledge/Comprehension, Application/Analysis, Creation/Evaluation). Scaffold thinking toward standard mastery per HQIM guidance.
key_terms.Knowledge and Comprehension Questions: Ask for student recall of basic knowledge facts aligned to standard.
key_terms.Application and Analysis Questions: Require students to apply understanding to similar concepts/scenarios.
key_terms.Creation and Evaluation Questions: Require students to synthesize learning and transfer to create meaning.
key_terms.Purposeful: Intentionally build on students’ learning and understanding of objective.
key_terms.Sequenced: How teacher orders questions strategically to scaffold understanding.
key_terms.Rigor: Continuously engaged in rigorous/critical thinking, constructing understanding at deep level, allowing productive struggle.
key_terms.Active Responses: Require all students to engage (whole group, turn/talk, white boards). Safe environment needed.
key_terms.Wait Time: Appropriate time between question/response creates opportunity for all to engage in thinking.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Teacher questions are varied and high-quality, providing an appropriate mix of question types based on content: knowledge and comprehension; application and analysis; and creation and evaluation.
Questions are consistently purposeful and coherent.
The frequency of questions consistently engages students in the rigor of the content and in critical thinking.
Questions are consistently sequenced with attention to the instructional goals.
Wait time (3-5 seconds) is consistently provided.
Students regularly respond to a variety of teacher questions (e.g., whole-class signaling, choral responses, written and shared responses, or group and individual answers).
All students are actively answering questions and engaging with the teacher or each other to share their perspectives.
Students generate questions that lead to further inquiry and self-directed learning.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher questions are varied and high-quality...
descriptor_details.explanation: Requires understanding standard/objective rigor and how questions prompt/scaffold thinking. Note impact of higher-order questions on Thinking/Problem-Solving indicators. Strive for varied, scaffolded, leveled questions.
possible_evidence: Questions scaffold from basic recall to higher-order thinking

descriptor_details.descriptor: Questions are consistently purposeful and coherent.
descriptor_details.explanation: Creates opportunities for feedback on depth of learning. Strengthen practice by adjusting instruction based on responses without lowering rigor.
possible_evidence: Questions directly relate to lesson objective
Teacher uses responses to gauge understanding

descriptor_details.descriptor: The frequency of questions consistently engages students in the rigor...
descriptor_details.explanation: Consistent engagement in critical thinking maintains rigor and provides continuous opportunities to deepen learning. Allow productive struggle.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Questions are consistently sequenced...
descriptor_details.explanation: Use responses as formative assessment to determine mastery. Plan questions based on HQIM guidance.
possible_evidence: Teacher uses questioning patterns from HQIM

descriptor_details.descriptor: Wait time (3-5 seconds) is consistently provided.
descriptor_details.explanation: Essential to label wait time so students understand its role in creating positive environment. Connects to Respectful Conditions.
possible_evidence: Sufficient pause between question and expecting response
All students appear to be thinking

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students regularly respond to a variety of teacher questions...
descriptor_details.explanation: Require active responses from each student to monitor understanding for all. Use combination of total participation techniques and individual responses.
possible_evidence: Use of choral response, think-pair-share, whiteboards
Teacher calls on variety of students (random selection)

descriptor_details.descriptor: All students are actively answering questions and engaging...
descriptor_details.explanation: Utilize methods ensuring every student responds/engages. Avoids calling only on volunteers/same students. Multiple perspectives shared/valued when environment is safe/respectful.
possible_evidence: Students respond to/build on peers' answers

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students generate questions that lead to further inquiry...
descriptor_details.explanation: Root questions in HQIM guidance to ensure rigor toward mastery. Includes opportunities for students to generate own questions. Model question types (Bloom's, DOK). Provide choices.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Teacher questions are varied and high-quality, providing an appropriate mix of question types based on content: knowledge and comprehension; application and analysis; and creation and evaluation.
Questions are purposeful and coherent.
The frequency of questions engages students in critical thinking.
Questions are sequenced with attention to the instructional goals.
Wait time (3-5 seconds) is provided.
Questions require active responses (e.g., whole-class signaling, choral responses, or group and individual answers).
The teacher calls on a variety of students to engage different students’ perspectives and provide opportunities for many students to respond.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Teacher questions are inconsistent in quality and include few question types: knowledge and comprehension; application and analysis; and creation and evaluation.
Questions are random and lack coherence.
The frequency of questions sometimes engages students in critical thinking.
Questions are rarely sequenced with attention to the instructional goals.
Wait time (3-5 seconds) is inconsistently provided.
Questions rarely require active responses (e.g., whole-class signaling, choral responses, or group and individual answers).
The teacher mostly calls on volunteers.

suggested_coaching_questions: Why is it essential for you to ask higher-order questions during a lesson?
How will you plan for questions that increase rigor and student ownership?
How will you decide on the types and frequency of questions asked during a lesson?
Why is it essential to plan intentional questions aligned to the lesson's standard/expected outcome/objective?
What types of questions might you need to ask to gather evidence of students' thinking?
How will you provide opportunities for all students to respond to your questions?
How will you ensure that all students have opportunities to answer questions and discuss responses and perspectives with one another?
How will you ensure that students have the opportunity to interact with each other about their learning?
How will you ensure wait time is provided for all students during a lesson?
How will you model ways to generate self-directed questions aligned to the learning for students?
Why is it essential for students to have opportunities to develop their own questions and search for the answers?

indicators.overview: How teachers respond to student comments/questions. Addresses quality of feedback supporting learning (not just accuracy). Deepest learning when meaning constructed by learner. Effective feedback prompts thinking.
indicators.content_connections: Use academic vocabulary from standards/content. Respond to attempts/responses with similar vocabulary.
student_centered_evidence: Evidence student proficiency increases due to feedback.
Students seek teacher/peer feedback.
Students use feedback to improve learning/work.
Students provide peer feedback using success criteria language.
Students engage in academic conversations with curriculum.
Students accept, internalize, modify understanding based on feedback.
Students articulate how feedback helps them understand learning process/improvement needs.
Students hold self/others accountable by formulating/sharing feedback.
Students use feedback to self-monitor learning/progression.
Students understand/articulate role of feedback.

key_terms.Focused, Frequent, and of High Quality: High-quality feedback: explicitly aligned to student learning (considers success criteria), causes student thinking toward mastery, timely (throughout lesson), brings attention to academic language.
key_terms.Circulation: Teacher walking around, listening during individual/pair/group work. Allows asking/answering questions, listening, providing feedback.
key_terms.Teacher-to-Student Feedback: Teacher-led, models feedback for students. Rooted in academic language of standard/objective/expectations.
key_terms.Student-to-Student Feedback: Student-led. Characteristic of student-owned environment valuing critical thinking. Rooted in academic language.
key_terms.Student-to-Teacher Feedback: What teacher gains (verbal/non-verbal) letting teacher know what's learned, informing next steps.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Oral and written feedback is consistently academically focused, frequent, and high-quality.
Feedback is frequently given during guided practice, throughout the lesson, and during review of independent work assignments.
The teacher circulates during instructional activities to prompt student thinking, assess each student’s progress based on student work expectations, and provide individual feedback.
Feedback, both verbal and non-verbal, from students is regularly used to monitor and adjust instruction.
Students give specific and clear feedback to each other based on the teacher’s expectations.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Oral and written feedback is consistently academically focused, frequent, and high quality.
descriptor_details.explanation: High-quality feedback relates to objective/sub-objectives, causes thinking, is specific, timely, varied, rooted in academic language of standards/objective/expectations. Oral and/or written.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Feedback is frequently given during guided practice...
descriptor_details.explanation: Cornerstone for understanding/mastery. Plan feedback at critical points. Consider process and product success criteria. Model high-quality feedback for students.
possible_evidence: Feedback provided during multiple lesson phases

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher circulates during instructional activities...
descriptor_details.explanation: Walk around, listen to conversations. Listen for key phrases indicating misconceptions or on-track learning. Provide aligned feedback prompting thinking (aligned to success criteria). Requires clarity on learning progression.
possible_evidence: Teacher moves around room during work time
Teacher provides targeted feedback to individuals/groups based on observations

descriptor_details.descriptor: Feedback, both verbal and non-verbal, from students is regularly used...
descriptor_details.explanation: Teacher asks questions aligned to objective/success criteria. When answers inaccurate, prepare to reteach/explain differently.
possible_evidence: Teacher uses student responses/questions to adjust instruction
Teacher reteaches concepts based on feedback

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students give specific and clear feedback to each other...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students effectively prompt each other's thinking when success criteria/expectations are clear and model for feedback provided.
possible_evidence: Students use success criteria language in peer feedback
Peer feedback is specific and constructive
Teacher has modeled effective peer feedback

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Oral and written feedback is academically focused, frequent, and high-quality.
Feedback is given during guided practice, throughout the lesson, and during review of independent work assignments.
The teacher circulates during instructional activities to support engagement and monitor student work.
Feedback from students is used to monitor and adjust instruction.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The quality and timeliness of feedback is inconsistent.
Feedback is sometimes given during guided practice.
The teacher circulates during instructional activities but monitors mostly behavior.
Feedback from students is sometimes used to monitor or adjust instruction.

suggested_coaching_questions: How can you be sure the academic feedback you provide prompts student thinking toward mastery of the objective?
How can you be sure the academic feedback you provide helps students identify the strengths and next steps in their work?
How will you move from corrective feedback to feedback that empowers students?
At what points in the lesson will you be gaining feedback from your students to inform the next steps of instruction?
What will you look and listen for as you circulate the classroom?
How will you know if your students have misconceptions about the content or if they are on-track in their learning? What will you do about it?
How will you use student feedback to adjust your instruction?
How can you create opportunities for students to provide academic feedback to each other to deepen their learning?
How can you ensure that the student-to-student feedback is aligned to the standard and learning expectations (success criteria) to master the objective?
What will you expect to hear in the student-to-student feedback as evidence of high-quality feedback and what will you need to do first to ensure that it takes place?
How will you structure protocols for student-to-student feedback?
Where in the lesson are opportune times for students to self-assess in relation to the lesson's success criteria and expectations?
How will students use feedback to monitor their own learning and progression toward their goals?

indicators.overview: Addresses instructional arrangements. Focuses on how students grouped and held accountable.
indicators.content_connections: Structure lessons for peer learning opportunities. Ensure collaboration aligned to standard/content rigor. Reference collaborative practices from HQIM (small group discussions, activities, skill practice).
student_centered_evidence: Students explain expectations for grouping arrangements.
Students ask questions/seek clarification on group role/task/expectations.
Students clarify/commit to individual roles and consequences.
Students set goals, reflect/evaluate learning during group/individual activities.
Students take initiative to develop plan to solve task/problem.
Students complete work meeting expectations individually/as group.
Students reflect on progress toward mastery within group/individually.

key_terms.Grouping Arrangements: Student grouping compositions (individual, partner, small groups 3-5, whole group). Intentionality needed. Deeply connected to TKS.
key_terms.Efficiency: Knowledge gained as result of instruction, activity, discussion toward mastery.
key_terms.Expectations: Intentional use of learning targets and pathway to mastery.
key_terms.Accountability: Student takes responsibility for role (individual/collective). Seeks clarity, commits to task, understands part in bigger picture.
key_terms.Varied: Teacher considers lesson goal, plans mixed compositions for access to deep thinking/learning for all.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: The instructional grouping arrangements (whole class, small groups, pairs, or individual) consistently maximize student understanding and learning efficiency.
Teacher sets clear expectations that are understood by students.
In an instructional group, each student takes responsibility for their individual role, tasks, and group work expectations so they can have meaningful and productive collaboration.
In an instructional group, each student assumes accountability for completing group work and individual work.
Instructional group composition is varied to best accomplish the goals of the lesson.
Students set goals, reflect on, and evaluate their learning in instructional groups.
When provided the choice or independence, students make responsible decisions about how to group themselves.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The instructional grouping arrangements... consistently maximize student understanding...
descriptor_details.explanation: Instructional grouping used to: ensure all learn, increase engagement, promote social/collaborative skills, promote peer feedback, engage critical thinking, engage problem-solving. Specific purpose needed, contributing to positive outcomes. Task determines arrangement type. Requires clear understanding of intentions, curriculum recs, interaction level, meaningful roles.
possible_evidence: Group tasks aligned with learning objective

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher sets clear expectations that are understood by students.
descriptor_details.explanation: Includes expectations for procedures and behavior during grouping. Models may include visuals, demos, rubrics, steps. Expectations for each member and group as whole clearly explained. Procedures for materials, noise level etc. clearly explained.
possible_evidence: Anchor chart for group work norms/roles

descriptor_details.descriptor: In an instructional group, each student takes responsibility...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students know what's expected for their role. Listen and can repeat assigned title/summary. Gather resources, perform functions with little direction. Open to peer feedback.
possible_evidence: Students hold each other accountable within group

descriptor_details.descriptor: In an instructional group, each student assumes accountability...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students ask clarifying questions, monitor time. Show commitment via active participation, engagement, reflection. Understand contribution of task to outcome.
possible_evidence: Active participation from all group members

descriptor_details.descriptor: Instructional group composition is varied...
descriptor_details.explanation: Carefully planned compositions encourage interaction, friendship, harmony. Varying ability levels (if appropriate) provide examples of assisting behaviors.
possible_evidence: Group composition changes based on task/goal
Teacher considers student dynamics in grouping

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students set goals, reflect on, and evaluate their learning...
descriptor_details.explanation: Exemplifies student ownership. Students set personal learning goals, understand expectations/criteria. Aware of expectations while learning. Set goals, provide peer feedback, self-assess, adjust work.
possible_evidence: Groups set collective goals for task

descriptor_details.descriptor: When provided the choice or independence, students make responsible decisions...
descriptor_details.explanation: Benefits: increased ownership/quality. Teacher must explicitly communicate expectations (roles, responsibilities, outcome, time). Teach students responsible decision-making (consider strengths, knowledge, goals, growth areas).
possible_evidence: Students choose groups based on task requirements
Teacher provides guidance on making responsible group choices

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: The instructional grouping arrangements (whole class, small groups, pairs, or individual) adequately enhance student understanding and learning efficiency.
Teacher sets expectations that are understood by students.
In an instructional group, students take responsibility for their roles, tasks, and group work expectations so they can have meaningful and productive collaboration.
Students participating in groups are held accountable for group work and individual work.
Instructional group composition is varied to accomplish the goals of the lesson.
Instructional groups facilitate opportunities for students to set goals, reflect on, and evaluate their learning.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The instructional grouping arrangements (whole class, small groups, pairs, or individual) inhibit student understanding and learning efficiency.
Few students in groups know their roles, responsibilities, and group work expectations.
Few students participating in groups are held accountable for group work and individual work.
Instructional group composition remains unchanged, irrespective of the learning and instructional goals of a lesson.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you decide on the instructional grouping of students during a lesson?
How does the type of activity or segment within a lesson impact the instructional grouping for that activity or segment?
Why is it important to think about how you group students in a lesson? That being said, what are things you consider when forming groups (or partners) and why?
How can you ensure students know what is expected of them so they can take responsibility for their individual roles?
How can you ensure each role is meaningful and students assume accountability for completing their task(s)?
How do you model or communicate your expectations to students for their own work and that of the group? How do you check for understanding of the expectations?
How do you assess the performance of groups and individuals when work is completed in a group setting?
How do you teach students to make responsible decisions when given the choice to choose their own group?
How will you ensure that the instructional grouping arrangement and assigned tasks are appropriately rigorous for each member of the group?
How will you leverage instructional grouping arrangements to promote student ownership in this lesson?

indicators.overview: Teacher's knowledge of content/HQIM and ability to implement appropriate strategies. Ability to connect content to other ideas/concepts.
indicators.content_connections: HQIM/standards provide solid content understanding. Deepen by reviewing all materials/resources, collaborating. Results in more profound student learning.
student_centered_evidence: Students communicate how HQIM supports build understanding.
Students label own thinking applying lesson model.
Students clear on objective, development, mastery requirements.
Students make conceptual connections within/across content areas.
Students appropriately/independently use strategies.
Students understand relevance, recognize applicability.

key_terms.Content Understanding: Deeper than language: prerequisite skills, learning progressions, relationships/nuances within content/materials/standards, what mastery looks like at highest rigor.
key_terms.Subject-Specific Instructional Strategie: How content knowledge effectively taught/learned. Requires deep understanding of HQIM, utilizing rigorous conceptual strategies.
key_terms.Key Concepts: Critical foundational ideas conceptually connecting to powerful ideas within/beyond content. Requires expert understanding of standards, skills, criteria, big ideas.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Teacher displays extensive content knowledge and understanding of both state standards and high-quality instructional materials, including their adopted or approved curriculum, for all the subjects they teach.
Teacher consistently implements a variety of subject-specific instructional strategies to enhance student content knowledge.
Teacher consistently highlights key concepts and ideas and uses them as the basis to connect other powerful ideas.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher displays extensive content knowledge...
descriptor_details.explanation: Includes understanding standards, mastery criteria, extensive depth in HQIM. Use this knowledge to plan compelling experiences. Display via: using HQIM resources aligned to rigor, following intentions/guidance; connecting purpose to elements; sharing why/how objective connects to life/future learning; having students preview.
possible_evidence: Lesson connects to real-world applications/future learning

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher consistently implements a variety of subject-specific instructional strategies...
descriptor_details.explanation: Know how to identify/implement specific strategies enhancing learning for particular lesson, aligned to purpose. Evidence: focused presentation (model, examples, analogies, visuals); sequenced questions scaffolding knowledge; selection/implementation of activities/materials supporting progression; integration of thinking/problem-solving.
possible_evidence: Use of varied instructional strategies observed

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher consistently highlights key concepts and ideas...
descriptor_details.explanation: Expertly connect big ideas to other powerful, relevant ideas. Examples: utilize universal themes/generalizations across units/disciplines; connect lesson ideas to unit key concepts for transfer; reference/use prompts about current events/culture.
possible_evidence: Explicit connections made between lesson and unit themes
Discussions link content to broader ideas/current events

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Teacher displays accurate content knowledge and understanding of both state standards and high-quality instructional materials, including their adopted or approved curriculum, for all the subjects they teach.
Teacher implements subject-specific instructional strategies to enhance student content knowledge.
Teacher highlights key concepts and ideas and uses them as the basis to connect other powerful ideas.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Teacher displays underdeveloped content knowledge and lacks understanding of state standards or high-quality instructional materials, including their adopted or approved curriculum, in several subject areas.
Teacher rarely implements subject-specific instructional strategies to enhance student content knowledge.
Teacher does not understand key concepts and ideas in the discipline and therefore presents content in an unconnected way.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you prepare yourself to teach (insert the specific topic taught)?
How will you use the high-quality curricular materials available to you and your students?
How will you know the subject-specific instructional strategies within the curriculum enhance student learning?
How will you connect key concepts in the content being taught to more powerful ideas within the content and other disciplines?
What are some other ideas to which you could have connected during the lesson?
How will you ensure the content being learned in this lesson is appropriately rigorous for all learners?
How can you leverage the content and curriculum to promote student ownership?

indicators.overview: How well teacher knows students, learning styles, interests. Connects to Motivating Students. Know how students best motivated, support progress. Ability to organize content motivating/connecting to interests/contexts essential. Plan meaningful learning aligned to background/interests, use knowledge to scaffold.
indicators.content_connections: HQIM often include recommendations for differentiated supports/strategies. Resources for intervention, remediation, acceleration, extension/challenge, EL support. Analyze data, identify appropriate resources. Planning use is essential. Curricular resources include connections to backgrounds/interests.
student_centered_evidence: Students engage with varying supports to demonstrate mastery.
Students connect with learning, desire to engage.
Students persist in work, rigorous learning.
Students work respectfully in varied groupings.
Students learn with/from others collaboratively.
Early finishers engage in HQ extension activities.

key_terms.Anticipated Learning Abilities and Needs: Obstacles students might face accessing learning needed for mastery, identified/planned for by teacher before lesson.
key_terms.Differentiated Supports and Strategies: Design of lessons with intentional methods meeting diverse academic needs. Continual assessment/adjustment.
key_terms.Interests, Backgrounds: What students like/care about (Interests). Context of home lives, relationships, prior knowledge (Backgrounds).

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Teacher practices display understanding of each student’s anticipated learning abilities and needs.
Teacher practices consistently incorporate student interests and backgrounds.
Teacher consistently provides differentiated supports and strategies to ensure students have the opportunity to master grade-level standards.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher practices display understanding of each student’s anticipated learning abilities and needs.
descriptor_details.explanation: Teachers design instruction addressing needs. Consider potential struggles before lesson.
possible_evidence: Lesson plan includes notes on anticipated student difficulties

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher practices consistently incorporate student interests and backgrounds.
descriptor_details.explanation: Connect content to student interests/backgrounds making it personally meaningful/relevant. Connect existing schemas to content.
possible_evidence: Lesson topics/examples relate to student interests
Student choice offered based on interests

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher consistently provides differentiated supports and strategies...
descriptor_details.explanation: Utilize alternative strategies for mastery. Make content accessible (learning, visual, auditory needs) without removing from essential subject matter. Embed opportunities for different progress rates (extension/streamlined). Differentiation shouldn't change rigor.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Teacher practices display understanding of students’ anticipated learning abilities and needs.
Teacher practices incorporate student interests and backgrounds.
Teacher provides differentiated supports and strategies to ensure students have the opportunity to master grade-level standards.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Teacher practices demonstrate some knowledge of students’ anticipated learning abilities and needs.
Teacher practices sometimes incorporate student interests or backgrounds.
Teacher practices demonstrate some differentiation.

suggested_coaching_questions: What learning challenges do you anticipate for your students in this lesson? What type of support will your students need?
How do you identify your students’ interests and backgrounds and incorporate these into your lessons?
How do you plan for and provide differentiated supports and strategies within your lessons?
How will you determine which students are ready for today's content, which need additional support, and which need additional challenge?
How will you provide differentiated instruction to ensure every student is met where they are and taken to the next level of learning?
How will you provide opportunities for all learners to have ownership of their learning in this lesson?

indicators.overview: Developing multiple thinking/problem-solving skills enriches ability to manage complex tasks/higher learning. Thinking is process, problem-solving is product. Teacher empowers students by providing practice opportunities. Requires teaching the thinking/problem-solving types.
indicators.content_connections: HQIM provide activities, questions, strategies prompting thinking/problem-solving. May feature activities making thinking visible (graphic organizers, thinking maps). Plan how to model thinking, use curriculum components.
student_centered_evidence: Students persevere through challenging tasks applying thinking models.
Students support responses with justification/reasoning.
Students identify/discuss individual progress toward mastery.
Students make appropriate learning decisions supporting own thinking.
Students aware of multiple aspects, consider different perspectives.
Students actively use success criteria, compare to work, make adjustments.
Students talk with peers/teacher about thinking strategies used/why beneficial.

key_terms.Thinking: Metacognitive; awareness/understanding of own thought processes necessary to process/apply content knowledge.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Students are actively engaged in multiple types of thinking: analytical thinking, where students analyze, compare and contrast, and evaluate and explain information; practical thinking, where students use, apply, and implement what they learn in real-life scenarios; creative thinking, where students create, design, imagine, and suppose; and research-based thinking, where students explore and review a variety of ideas, models, and solutions to problems.
The teacher and/or students model metacognitive strategies.

Students are provided opportunities to: generate a variety of ideas and alternatives; analyze problems from multiple perspectives and viewpoints; and monitor their thinking to ensure they understand what they are learning, are attending to critical information, and are aware of the learning strategies they are using and why.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students are actively engaged in multiple types of thinking: analytical...
descriptor_details.explanation: Analytical: deeply examine aspects/parts; analyze, evaluate, explain phenomena. Practical: apply skills/knowledge to own lives; see connections school/real world. Creative: develop new ideas/products connected to content/concepts. Research-based: examine info from multiple sources to solve problem; review ideas, find well-supported solutions.
possible_evidence: Students apply learning to real-world problems
Students synthesize information from multiple sources

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher and/or students model metacognitive strategies.
descriptor_details.explanation: Make thinking visible by modeling metacognitive strategies, opening up thought process steps. Supports students' own thinking.
possible_evidence: Use of graphic organizers to map thinking

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students are provided opportunities to: generate a variety of ideas...
descriptor_details.explanation: Generate ideas/alternatives: consider topic multiple ways, deeper understanding. Analyze from multiple perspectives: learn how others view problems/solutions. Monitor thinking: supports deeper engagement/performance; apply learning independently.
possible_evidence: Debates or discussions exploring multiple viewpoints
Students reflect on/articulate their learning strategies

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: The teacher engages students in multiple types of thinking: analytical thinking, where students analyze, compare and contrast, and evaluate and explain information; practical thinking, where students use, apply, and implement what they learn in real-life scenarios; creative thinking, where students create, design, imagine, and suppose; and research-based thinking, where students explore and review a variety of ideas, models, and solutions to problems.
The teacher and students: generate a variety of ideas and alternatives; and analyze problems from multiple perspectives and viewpoints.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The teacher implements some learning experiences that engage students in different types of thinking.
The teacher sometimes provides opportunities where students: generate a variety of ideas and alternatives; or analyze problems from multiple perspectives and viewpoints.

suggested_coaching_questions: How can you model your thinking for students so that it supports their own metacognition in their progression toward lesson mastery?
How do you plan for activities and/or assignments that provide students with the opportunity to apply their thinking?
How can you incorporate opportunities for students to apply analytical, creative, practical and research-based thinking?
What metacognitive process will the activities and student work require of students?
Where in the lesson will you release the thinking to the students? What do you expect to see and hear?

indicators.overview: Developing multiple problem-solving skills enriches ability to manage complex tasks/higher learning. Empowers students with life skill. Requires teaching the problem-solving types.
indicators.content_connections: HQIM provide activities, questions, strategies prompting thinking/problem-solving. Utilize student learning activities from adopted curriculums aligning to various problem-solving types.
student_centered_evidence: Students produce solutions engaging variety of thinking types.
Students create clear representations of problems via thinking application.
Students persist in deep engagement demonstrating satisfaction at solution.
Students produce products requiring thinking/understanding of specific concept/objective.

key_terms.Problem-solving: Products developed as result of applying thinking process to specific content-related task.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Students engage in activities that reinforce several of the following problem-solving types: Abstraction, Categorization, Drawing conclusions/justifying solutions, Predicting outcomes, Observing and experimenting, Improving solutions, Identifying relevant/irrelevant information, Generating ideas, Creating and designing

descriptor_details.descriptor: Abstraction
descriptor_details.explanation: Understand concepts not tied to physical experience. Apply abstract thinking, absorb info, connect to larger concepts. Analyze inputs for common theme/conjecture.
possible_evidence: Students identify themes across multiple texts
Students derive general rules from specific examples

descriptor_details.descriptor: Categorization
descriptor_details.explanation: Analyze, classify, sort info into meaningful categories. Allows analyzing content, categorizing new info for recall/future use.
possible_evidence: Students sort shapes based on properties
Students classify historical events by cause/effect

descriptor_details.descriptor: Drawing conclusions/justifying solutions
descriptor_details.explanation: Draw conclusions/inferences based on data (various forms/viewpoints/quality). Types: specific answer/idea/opinion; concept derived from content; objective look at thinking used. Justify by analyzing options, selecting best, proving why best.
possible_evidence: Students evaluate different solutions to a problem

descriptor_details.descriptor: Predicting outcomes
descriptor_details.explanation: Presented with info/input, make hypothesis/educated guess. Followed by observation, experimenting, drawing conclusions/justifying.
possible_evidence: Students predict results of science experiment
Students predict story endings based on evidence

descriptor_details.descriptor: Observing and experimenting
descriptor_details.explanation: Observe, record/code, measure. Make hypothesis, collect/analyze data aligned.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Improving solutions
descriptor_details.explanation: Given solution, suggest methods to improve/make better.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Identifying relevant/irrelevant information
descriptor_details.explanation: Given relevant/irrelevant info, identify relevant and use to solve problem.
possible_evidence: Students identify necessary info in word problems

descriptor_details.descriptor: Generating ideas
descriptor_details.explanation: Presented with problem, brainstorm lists of ideas/viable solutions.
possible_evidence: Generating multiple solutions to a math problem

descriptor_details.descriptor: Creating and designing
descriptor_details.explanation: Develop new/unique product other students can solve/evaluate.
possible_evidence: Students design board game based on literature unit

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: The teacher uses and/or engages students in some of the following problem-solving types: Abstraction, Categorization, Drawing conclusions/justifying solutions, Predicting outcomes, Observing and experimenting, Improving solutions, Identifying relevant/irrelevant information, Generating ideas, Creating and designing

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The teacher sometimes engages students in the following problem-solving types: Abstraction, Categorization, Drawing conclusions/justifying solutions, Predicting outcomes, Observing and experimenting, Improving solutions, Identifying relevant/irrelevant information, Generating ideas, Creating and designing

suggested_coaching_questions: What are the student work activities and products that students will engage in during a lesson?
What types of problem-solving do these student work products require? What types of thinking do these student work activities and products require?
How will students be actively engaged in problem-solving to demonstrate understanding and mastery of the lesson objective?
How can your lessons provide opportunities for students to engage in a variety of types of problem-solving tasks?

indicators.overview: Contribute to effective/efficient learning, engaged classrooms. Based on standards, HQIM, assessment analysis. Incorporate standards, curriculum, assessments in daily/weekly/unit planning. Tightly connected across domains. Plan with end in mind (objective), then how students demonstrate mastery (Student Work/Assessment), then activities/materials.
indicators.content_connections: Foundation of impactful teaching/learning. Align with standards, incorporate HQIM. Annotate scripted lessons for individual/group needs without changing rigor. Annotations: highlight keys, use examples, scaffold questions, include/skip activities, connect materials, denote groupings, list supports.
student_centered_evidence: Students understand objectives/connection to standards.
Students authentically engage in activities.
Students make connections background knowledge/activities/materials.
Students understand how new learning builds on prior/integrates.
Students demonstrate autonomy/ownership via choices.
Students reflect on progress toward mastery/objective/criteria.
Students complete assigned activities/assessments.

key_terms.Curriculum: Set of lessons delivering targets (texts, materials, content, resources). HQ includes high expectations, standard alignment, rigor.
key_terms.Relevant: Plans include activities/materials students identify/recognize as familiar.
key_terms.Integrate: Planning meaningful/connected learning across content areas.
key_terms.Student Work: Measurable products from standards-based activities making thinking/learning visible.
key_terms.Reflection: Students think about learning accomplished and progress toward objectives against criteria.
key_terms.Closure: Time at end of segment reviewing what learned.
