key_terms.Annotated: Taking notes enhancing/drawing attention to critical curriculum components during planning.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: evidence of the internalization of the plans from the high-quality curriculum;
measurable and explicit objectives aligned to state standards and aligned high-quality curriculum, both in content and in rigor;

activities, materials, and assessments that: are aligned to state standards; content, including high-quality curriculum; and success criteria; are sequenced and scaffolded based on student need; build on prior student knowledge, are relevant to students’ lives, and integrate other disciplines as appropriate; and provide appropriate time for student work, student reflection, and lesson closure;
evidence that the plan is appropriate for the age, knowledge, and interests of all learners;
evidence that the plan provides regular opportunities to accommodate individual student needs; and
strategies for student autonomy and ownership.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Evidence of the internalization of the plans...
descriptor_details.explanation: Deep understanding of standards/curriculum to internalize intentions. Often displayed via annotations (anticipated misconceptions, working through problems).
possible_evidence: Lesson plan annotations showing teacher thinking

descriptor_details.descriptor: Measurable and explicit objectives aligned to state standards...
descriptor_details.explanation: Use standards-aligned scope/sequence for planning. Annotate provided plans (identify success criteria, cue actions, plan questions, enhance). Daily plans need explicit objective (know/understand/do). Provides destination for roadmap of activities.
possible_evidence: Objective clearly stated, measurable, aligned to standard

descriptor_details.descriptor: Activities, materials, and assessments that: are aligned...
descriptor_details.explanation: Should be aligned to standard(s), address curriculum intentions, model expectations, provide practice time, connect background knowledge. Ensure students are center of plan, include reflection time.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Evidence that the plan is appropriate for the age, knowledge, and interests...
descriptor_details.explanation: Address how teacher motivates engagement. Know students, plan connections between content/interests.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Evidence that the plan provides regular opportunities to accommodate...
descriptor_details.explanation: Explicitly outline intentional differentiation meeting diverse needs, ensuring access to grade-level standards. Observe via rich/engaging activities with meaningful application opportunities.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Strategies for student autonomy and ownership.
descriptor_details.explanation: Clearly label intentional/purposeful structures facilitating autonomy/ownership.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: some evidence of the internalization of the plans from the high-quality curriculum;
objectives aligned to state standards and aligned high-quality curriculum, both in content and in rigor;

activities, materials, and assessments that: are aligned to state standards; content, including high-quality curriculum; and success criteria; are sequenced and scaffolded based on student need; build on prior student knowledge; and provide appropriate time for student work and lesson closure;
evidence that the plan is appropriate for the age, knowledge, and interests of learners; and
evidence that the plan provides opportunities to accommodate individual student needs.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: little evidence of the internalization of the plans from the high-quality curriculum;
some objectives aligned to state standards and aligned high-quality curriculum;

activities, materials, and assessments that: are sometimes aligned to state standards; are sometimes logically sequenced; sometimes build on prior student knowledge; and inconsistently provide time for student work and lesson closure;
little evidence that the plan is appropriate for the age, knowledge, or interests of the learners; and
little evidence that the plan provides opportunities to accommodate individual student needs.

suggested_coaching_questions: What annotations do you need to make in your curriculum guides and lesson plans to support mastery for your students?
What do you want your students to be able to do as a result of your teaching?
How will students show/demonstrate what they have learned?
How will you set student-centered goals that are aligned to the state standards?
What student engagement strategies will work best with the lesson you are planning?
How will you ensure that all activities, materials, and assessments are aligned to the lesson learning objective, are age appropriate, and pique the interests of all learners?
How will you intentionally plan to incorporate opportunities to accommodate individual student learning needs?
How will students have autonomy and ownership of their learning?
How will you provide appropriate time for student work, student reflection, and lesson closure?

indicators.overview: Effective planning requires considering content-specific work/assignments. Ensure challenge/rigor, align to standards, use HQIM, have clear success criteria. Work should allow multiple problem-solving/thinking types. Analyze work against criteria for future decisions.
indicators.content_connections: Design strong work ensuring alignment to standards, HQIM, success criteria. Identify assignments in HQIM requiring multiple thinking/problem-solving types, provide connection opportunities.
student_centered_evidence: Students engage in challenging work requiring variety of thinking.
Assignments prompt deep thinking beyond recall/reproduction.
Students write about content-area thinking.
Assignments provide opportunities for connections to own lives.

key_terms.Student Work: Measurable products from standards-based learning activities making student thinking/learning visible.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Assignments are: always aligned to the rigor and depth of the standards and curriculum content.
Assignments are: always aligned to the lesson’s objective and include descriptions of how assessment results will inform future instruction.
Students: organize, interpret, analyze, synthesize, and evaluate information rather than reproduce it;
Students: draw conclusions, make generalizations, and produce arguments that are supported through extended writing; and
Students: connect what they are learning to experiences, observations, feelings, or situations significant in their daily lives, both inside and outside of school.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assignments are always aligned to the rigor and depth...
descriptor_details.explanation: Student work aligned to rigor/depth provides clear understanding of learning. Impactful work intentionally planned/implemented with students at center. Analyzing products shows clear link to content/grade-level standards. Requires challenging/rigorous thinking.
possible_evidence: Student work matches complexity of standard
Clear link between assignment and standard

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assignments are always aligned to the lesson’s objective...
descriptor_details.explanation: Work aligned to objectives supports teacher analysis of mastery at standard's rigor level. Should be part of logical learning continuum, provide clear direction for subsequent lessons.
possible_evidence: Teacher uses assignment results to plan next steps
Assignment fits logically within unit sequence

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students: organize, interpret, analyze, synthesize, and evaluate...
descriptor_details.explanation: Assignments prompt deeper thinking than copying/guessing/reproducing. Provide perseverance opportunities via scaffolded assignments building deep content learning.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students draw conclusions, make generalizations, and produce arguments...
descriptor_details.explanation: Assignments prompt considering multiple info pieces, thinking deeply. Work results in content/grade-level specific writing making thinking visible.
possible_evidence: Students synthesize information to form conclusions

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students connect what they are learning to experiences...
descriptor_details.explanation: Assignments provide opportunities to consider how content connects to own experiences, adding deeper meaning/engagement.
possible_evidence: Students relate content to personal experiences/observations

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Assignments are: aligned to the rigor and depth of the standards and curriculum content.
Assignments are: aligned to the lesson’s objective and include descriptions of how assessment results will inform future instruction.
Assignments require students to: interpret information rather than reproduce it;
Assignments require students to: draw conclusions and support them through writing; and
Assignments require students to: connect what they are learning to prior learning and life experiences.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Assignments require students to: mostly reproduce information;
Assignments require students to: sometimes draw conclusions and support them through writing; and
Assignments require students to: sometimes connect what they are learning to prior learning or life experiences.

suggested_coaching_questions: How will you design opportunities for students to produce work that is aligned to the rigor and depth of the standards?
How can you use available high-quality curriculum materials to ensure student work assignments are aligned to the rigor and depth of the standards?
How will you plan to engage student thinking in organizing, interpreting, analyzing, synthesizing, and evaluating information rather than reproducing work?
How will you encourage students to engage in high-quality problem-solving so that they can draw conclusions, generalize, and produce arguments through extended writing assignments?
How will you create opportunities for students to connect what they are learning to experiences, observations, feelings, or situations in their daily lives?
How will you design student work assignments that encourage students to think beyond learning in the classroom?

indicators.overview: Fundamental part of instruction/learning. Effective plan answers: What do I want students to do? How do I know they learned? Regular asking/answering allows planning, diagnosing, intervening.
indicators.content_connections: Align to or take directly from HQIM. If unavailable, pay attention to scope/sequence/rigor. Classroom/school level data helps select subsequent standards/materials. Formative data generated during lesson.
student_centered_evidence: Students know what learning and how assessed.
Students self-monitor via metacognitive processes.
Students take ownership, self-assess based on clear criteria.
Students reference clear criteria throughout lesson.
Students ask self questions processing learning/checking understanding.

key_terms.Alignment: Assessments, objective, content, standards building/measuring same skill.
key_terms.State Standards: Knowledge/skills students expected to learn. Set clear benchmarks, guide teachers.
key_terms.Instructional Decisions: Systematic approach using achievement/other data for decisions during planning/delivery.
key_terms.Measurement Criteria: Define what success looks/sounds like, how assessed; defines mastery.
key_terms.Methods of Measuring Student Progress: Practices helping teachers use data/work evaluating teaching effectiveness, making informed decisions, identifying support needs.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher and Students Facilitate the Learning
descriptors: Assessments: are aligned with the depth and rigor of the state standards and content, including curriculum resources;
Assessments: are designed to provide feedback on progress against objectives;
Assessments: use a variety of question types and formats to gauge student learning and problem-solving;
Assessments: measure student performance in more than three ways (e.g., in the form of a project, experiment, presentation, essay, short answer, or multiple-choice);
Assessments: require extended written tasks as appropriate;
Assessments: include clear illustrations of student progress toward state standards, which students monitor, understand, and articulate; and
Assessments: include descriptions of how assessment results will be used by teachers and students to inform future instruction and learning.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments are aligned with the depth and rigor...
descriptor_details.explanation: Directly connected to activity/new learning. Align to standards, taken from HQIM (if available), aligned to objective per instructional plan.
possible_evidence: Clear link between assessment and objective

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments are designed to provide feedback...
descriptor_details.explanation: Plan must address how teacher collects data before/during/after lesson monitoring progress. Accomplished via formal checks for understanding (pre-planned moments).
possible_evidence: Teacher provides feedback based on assessment results
Students use feedback to adjust learning

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments use a variety of question types...
descriptor_details.explanation: Plan must include types of prompting questions used to gauge learning/problem-solving. Variety supports periodic checks. Understanding observable via questions/feedback.
possible_evidence: Mix of question formats (MC, short answer, essay, performance task)

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments measure student performance in more than three ways...
descriptor_details.explanation: Inclusion of formative/summative assessments allows tracking progress during/after lesson. Measures written in plans, include variety measuring impact.
possible_evidence: Multiple assessment methods used (project, test, presentation)
Variety reflects different ways students demonstrate understanding

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments require extended written tasks as appropriate.
descriptor_details.explanation: Extended written tasks prompt extending thinking and putting in writing.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments include clear illustrations of student progress...
descriptor_details.explanation: Clear illustration may look like student samples depicting performance levels aligned to success criteria.
possible_evidence: Rubrics clearly define criteria for success
Students can track own progress against standards

descriptor_details.descriptor: Assessments include descriptions of how assessment results will be used...
descriptor_details.explanation: Design informed by pre-assessment/baseline data (if available). Data informs next instructional steps for students/teacher.
possible_evidence: Lesson plan indicates how data will inform next steps
Teacher groups students based on assessment data

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/ Student Ownership of Learning – Teacher Facilitates the Learning
descriptors: Assessments: are aligned with the depth and rigor of the state standards and content, including curriculum resources;
Assessments: are designed to provide feedback on progress against objectives;
Assessments: use a variety of question types and formats to gauge student learning and problem-solving;
Assessments: measure student performance in more than two ways (e.g., in the form of a project, experiment, presentation, essay, short answer, or multiple choice);
Assessments: require written responses as appropriate; and
Assessments: include performance checks and student reflection on performance throughout the school year.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of Learning – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Assessments: are sometimes aligned with state standards and content, including curriculum resources;
Assessments: are not designed well to provide feedback on progress against objectives;
Assessments: use few question types to gauge student learning;
Assessments: measure student performance in less than two ways (e.g., in the form of a project, experiment, presentation, essay, short answer, or multiple choice); and
Assessments: include performance checks, although the purpose of these checks is not clear.

suggested_coaching_questions: How will you know the students learned what you taught?
How will you develop clear measurement criteria aligned to the state standards?
How will students demonstrate mastery through multiple measures (e.g., project, experiment, presentation, essay, short answer, or multiple-choice test)?
How will you use assessment to support the needs of individual students?
How will you check for understanding during the lesson? At the conclusion of the lesson?
How will you ensure that students understand how they are progressing and provide opportunities to support students’ self-awareness?

indicators.overview: Directly connects to Instruction domain. Fully exceed requires deep knowledge of students and standards/HQIM for clear/rigorous expectations. Students take active role leveraging expectations. Differentiated methods (rigorous, appropriate, success opportunities) require developed/utilized student knowledge.
indicators.content_connections: Clear/rigorous expectations aligned to grade-appropriate standards/objectives require fully understanding HQIM activities/materials ensuring access. Establish specific student-friendly criteria (mastery looks/sounds like). Teacher/students utilize criteria guiding expectations.
student_centered_evidence: Students encouraged self-monitor based on clear success criteria.
Students articulate progress, know what needed for success.
Students not afraid of mistakes, see as learning opportunities.
Students know successful when accomplish objective.
Students experience success due to differentiation.
Students persevere, strive to complete work.
Students not rushed, have opportunities to develop understanding.

key_terms.Rigorous Academic Expectations: Teacher communicates success/measurement criteria setting academic expectations. Rigor aligned to curriculum/grade-level standard(s). Students refer to expectations for self-assessment/monitoring.
key_terms.Describe Thinking: Students refer to success criteria, provide metacognition needed for task. Communicate strengths/weaknesses, strategies needed.
key_terms.Initiative: Teacher establishes/teaches/models processes students follow with little teacher direction. Students refer to criteria for self-monitoring.
key_terms.Optimizes: Teacher supports/strategies differentiated, allow different progress rates. Pacing efficient/effective for all. Planning/implementation allows access.
key_terms.Learning Goals: Students know daily goals, articulate progression using success criteria.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher and Students Establish the Environment
descriptors: Teacher engages students in learning with clear and rigorous academic expectations and actively uses aligned and differentiated high-quality materials and resources to ensure access to learning.
Students regularly learn from their mistakes and can describe their thinking on what they learned.
Teacher creates learning opportunities where all students consistently experience success.
Students lead opportunities that support learning.
Students take initiative to meet or exceed teacher expectations.
Teacher optimizes instructional time to ensure each student meets their learning goals.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher engages students in learning with clear and rigorous academic expectations...
descriptor_details.explanation: Teacher/student-generated success criteria developed. Teacher utilizes materials like diverse learners' guides, intervention lessons from standards-aligned curriculum.
possible_evidence: Differentiated materials used based on student needs

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students regularly learn from their mistakes...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students self-assess using success criteria, identify mistakes, self-correct, explain thinking changes, identify miscues.
possible_evidence: Students revise work based on feedback/self-assessment
Classroom culture supports risk-taking/learning from errors
Students articulate their thought process, including corrections

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher creates learning opportunities where all students consistently experience success.
descriptor_details.explanation: Teacher's pacing brisk, provides varied opportunities for gradual release based on needs. Explicit models for those needing them. Students access materials extending/clarifying learning based on self-assessment.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students lead opportunities that support learning.
descriptor_details.explanation: Students use success criteria aligned to objective, engage in variety of HQ materials. Support own learning via goal setting aligned to criteria.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students take initiative to meet or exceed teacher expectations.
descriptor_details.explanation: Teacher encourages tracking progress, setting goals for individual mastery. Students persevere by referring to criteria/strategies.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher optimizes instructional time...
descriptor_details.explanation: Teacher sets up experiences for enrichment (centers with aligned materials) or acceleration (small group, 1-on-1, intervention) supporting identified needs/understanding levels.
possible_evidence: Small group instruction targets specific needs

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher Establishes the Environment
descriptors: Teacher engages students in learning with clear and rigorous academic expectations and uses aligned high-quality materials and resources for students to access.
Teacher encourages students to learn from mistakes.
Teacher creates learning opportunities where all students can experience success.
Students complete their work according to teacher expectations.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Teacher expectations are not rigorous for students.
Teacher does not create learning opportunities where students can experience success.
Student work is rarely completed to meet teacher expectations.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you ensure that academic expectations for students are clear and rigorous? How are the academic expectations aligned to the grade-level standards?

What is the success criteria for learning? How are both the teacher and the students utilizing the criteria to monitor learning throughout the lesson? What adjustments are being made to ensure students have the opportunity to reach success? What feedback are students providing to one another? How are students making their thinking process visible?
Why is it important for students to have opportunities to learn from their mistakes? How are students working through their own mistakes and adjusting their learning?
How will you ensure that all students experience success with the lesson?
In the lesson, how will students take initiative and persevere with their own work?
In this lesson, how will students engage in goal setting?
How will you plan for activities that will optimize time for progression toward goals?

indicators.overview: Timely/effective management critical for instruction/learning. Connects to Instruction domain. Fully exceed requires environment where students understand own actions' impact. Self-aware, spend time completing assignments, engaged independently/collaboratively. Teacher establishes clear learning/behavior expectations, models.
indicators.content_connections: Critical for keeping focus on instruction. HQIM include embedded routines/structures. Critical teacher establishes/reinforces expectations minimizing lost time.
student_centered_evidence: Students/teacher determine class expectations/rules.
Students self-monitor behavior based on clear expectations/rules.
Students have/use coping strategies when frustrated.
Students actively display norms via actions.
Students provide positive feedback.
Students remind others when off task, quickly return.
Students support others' learning by reminding of expectations.

key_terms.Optimize: When students engaged in optimized learning, engaged in most effective learning strategies possible.
key_terms.Contingent Activities: High interest, engagement activities encouraging students, reinforcing behaviors, contributing to positive environment.
key_terms.Positive Reinforcement: Includes praising students for positive behaviors encouraging/reinforcing ideal behavior/interaction.
key_terms.Inconsequential Behavior: Behaviors bothersome to teacher but don't disrupt classroom environment.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher and Students Establish the Environment
descriptors: Students are consistently engaged in behaviors that optimize learning and increase time on task.
Teacher and students establish commitments for learning and behavior.

Teacher consistently uses, and students reinforce, several techniques (e.g., rewards, approval, contingent activities, consequences, etc.) that maintain student engagement and promote a positive classroom environment.
Teacher consistently recognizes and motivates positive behaviors and does not allow inconsequential behavior to interrupt the lesson.
Teacher addresses individual students who have caused disruptions rather than the entire class.
Teacher quickly attends to disruptions with minimal interruption to learning.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Students are consistently engaged in behaviors that optimize learning...
descriptor_details.explanation: Always cognitively/behaviorally engaged. No down time. Planning for consistent engagement/increased time on task minimizes off-task behavior. Teacher models explicit expectations, provides highly engaging/rigorous/relevant opportunities. Related to PIC and ACT indicators.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher and students establish commitments...
descriptor_details.explanation: Including students in establishing commitments communicates value for thoughts/voices. Ownership increases follow-through. Creates detailed understanding, less confusion. Active participation, brainstorming, critical thinking.
possible_evidence: Students remind peers of agreed-upon rules

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher consistently uses, and students reinforce, several techniques...
descriptor_details.explanation: Exemplary teachers do more than occasional engagement. Creating opportunities requires variety of techniques, student ownership. Rewards thoughtfully planned, follow-through essential. Students active participants, choice in rewards/contingencies. Outcome meaningful. Explicit communication of behaviors/consequences.
possible_evidence: Variety of positive reinforcement strategies used
Teacher connects incentives to specific positive behaviors

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher consistently recognizes and motivates positive behaviors...
descriptor_details.explanation: Hundreds of decisions daily. Consider overall impact vs. personal preference. If behavior bothersome but not impacting lesson/students, address individually later.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher addresses individual students who have caused disruptions...
descriptor_details.explanation: When inappropriate behavior damages environment, address it. Address student privately rather than whole class to avoid embarrassment/acting out.
possible_evidence: Focus remains on learning despite minor disruptions

descriptor_details.descriptor: The teacher quickly attends to disruptions...
descriptor_details.explanation: When disruption requires attention, address without major impact on learning. Address effectively with minimal time from instructional needs.
possible_evidence: Minimal instructional time lost to disruptions
Students quickly return to task after redirection

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher Establishes the Environment
descriptors: Students are mostly engaged in behaviors that optimize learning and increase time on task.
Teacher establishes rules for learning and behavior.
Teacher uses a variety of techniques (e.g., rewards, approval, contingent activities, consequences, etc.) that maintain student engagement and promote a positive classroom environment.
Teacher often recognizes and motivates positive behaviors and does not allow inconsequential behavior to interrupt the lesson.
Teacher addresses students who have caused disruptions, yet sometimes he or she addresses the entire class.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Students are consistently engaged in behavior that interrupts learning or minimizes time on task.
Teacher establishes few rules for learning and behavior.
Teacher uses few techniques to maintain student engagement.
Teacher does not or inconsistently addresses behavior that interrupts learning.
Teacher over-addresses inconsequential behavior.

suggested_coaching_questions: What strategies do you implement to encourage students to behave appropriately and stay on task during the lesson? How do you involve your students in this process?
How do you and your students establish class expectations, such as norms, contracts, and rules, to ensure learning is valued?
What are some techniques you and your students use to maintain appropriate individual and group behavior?
What types of behaviors do you deem inconsequential and often overlook?
How do you address specific students while not punishing the entire class?
Why is it important to attend to interruptions swiftly and firmly while teaching a lesson? How can this impact the learning of others?

indicators.overview: Key factor affecting learning. Connected to Instruction, Expectations, ESMB, RC. Fully exceed requires optimizing environment, including students in creation for community/inclusivity/empowerment. Positive/supportive for optimal learning. Students feel belong, welcome, trust, encouraged. Promotes intellectual risk taking.
indicators.content_connections: All students need access to grade-level content for accessible learning. Expectations set for all to master standards at rigor. HQIM resources used for scaffolds/interventions. Plan through lens of individual students without sacrificing integrity.
student_centered_evidence: Students work collaboratively, give/receive feedback.
Students choose how to utilize resources/tech.
Students produce work evidencing mastery.
Students reflect on progress individually/with others, ask questions.
Students curious, research further, question content.
Students attempt tasks outside comfort zone without fear.
Students engage in trial/error problem-solving collaboratively.

key_terms.Welcomes: All students feel belong, part of community. Non-members feel comfortable. All needs welcomed/supported.
key_terms.Safe: Free to express opinions, complete tasks, answer questions, provide peer feedback without fear.
key_terms.Accessible: Learning/resources organized so all know where to find. Learning differentiated for access based on style/level. Maximize learning. Same ease of access/opportunities for all.
key_terms.Opportunities: Provided tasks, support, collaborative structures allowing evidence of mastery. Able to own learning, push beyond.
key_terms.Student Work: Any product (say, do, make, write) showing evidence of mastery/progress. Includes verbal contributions.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher and Students Establish the Environment
descriptors: The classroom: welcomes all students and guests and provides a safe space for all students to take risks and interact with peers.
The classroom: is clearly organized and designed for and with students to promote learning for all.
The classroom: has supplies, equipment, and resources easily and readily accessible to provide opportunities for all students.
The classroom: displays current student work that promotes a positive classroom environment.
The classroom: is arranged to maximize individual and group learning and to reinforce a positive classroom environment.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The classroom: welcomes all students and guests...
descriptor_details.explanation: Students feel valued for individuality. Comfortable expressing opinions, attempting work without fear. Collaborative environment where everyone important. Encourage each other, debate using norms. Feedback freely given/received positively.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The classroom: is clearly organized and designed for and with students...
descriptor_details.explanation: Room arranged allowing all access to teacher/collaboration. Special considerations for seeing/hearing. Everyone feels centered.
possible_evidence: Teacher station accessible but not dominant

descriptor_details.descriptor: The classroom: has supplies, equipment, and resources easily and readily accessible...
descriptor_details.explanation: All students access needed supplies/equipment/resources to master content. Encouraged to utilize. Norms for accessing/returning allow timely use/little disruption.

descriptor_details.descriptor: The classroom: displays current student work...
descriptor_details.explanation: Work evidencing mastery/growth displayed/changed often. Students have voice in showcasing. Displayed work has positive feedback providing insight.
possible_evidence: Positive teacher/peer comments on displayed work

descriptor_details.descriptor: The classroom: is arranged to maximize individual and group learning...
descriptor_details.explanation: Room arranged for easy group/individual work without disruption. Space for teacher rotation, student access to teacher. Supplies/resources/tech housed/arranged for easy access. Positive messages, anchor charts posted. Goals posted/referenced. Targets/criteria visible/communicated/referenced.
possible_evidence: Furniture arrangement supports different grouping strategies

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher Establishes the Environment
descriptors: The classroom: welcomes all students and guests.
The classroom: is organized to promote learning for all students.
The classroom: has supplies, equipment, and resources accessible to provide opportunities for students.
The classroom: displays current student work.
The classroom: is arranged to promote individual and group learning.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: The classroom: is somewhat uninviting.
The classroom: is not organized to promote student learning.
The classroom: supplies, equipment, and resources are difficult to access.
The classroom: does not display student work.
The classroom: is not arranged to promote group learning.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do you ensure that all students in your classroom feel welcomed and that they are in a safe environment for learning and academic risk taking?
How do you organize your classroom so that all students have access to the supplies, technology, and other resources they need to master content?
Why is it important for all students to have their work showcased and displayed in the classroom? How do you determine which work to display?
How does your room arrangement help to create a positive classroom environment and maximize student collaboration and learning?
Why is it important for students to be able to take risks and how do you facilitate this in your classroom?
How do you ensure that a positive classroom environment is maintained?

indicators.overview: Respectful environment facilitates learning, connects to Instruction. Sustainable positive environment begins with respectful conditions. Fully exceed requires atmosphere beyond teacher-student interaction to mutual respect among students. More learning when feel safe/motivated/respected.
indicators.content_connections: Use HQIM/content inclusive of diverse backgrounds. Know student needs/abilities/interests for appropriate/engaging activities aligned to curriculum. Fosters respectful conditions, safe place.
student_centered_evidence: Students actively display expected norms (acknowledging viewpoints/ideas).
Students make positive personal connections throughout lessons.
Students respond non-prompted with affirmative comments/cheer.
Students comfortable respectfully challenging content/peer ideas.
Students feel safe expressing opinions/interests.
Students patient/respectful with each other.

key_terms.Interests and Opinions of All Students: Planning considers how all students best relate to content.
key_terms.Foster Positive Interactions: Teacher encourages/promotes effective communication skills among students.
key_terms.Receptive: Teacher willing consider/accept new suggestions/ideas from students.
key_terms.Interdependence: Students understand/recognize individual success linked to others'. Support/challenge each other for collective success.

Level_5_Exemplary.description_header: Consistent Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher and Students Establish the Environment
descriptors: Teacher-student and student-student interactions consistently demonstrate caring, kindness, and respect for one another and celebrate and acknowledge all students’ backgrounds.
Teacher seeks out and is receptive to the interests and opinions of all students.
Positive relationships and interdependence characterize the classroom.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher-student and student-student interactions consistently demonstrate caring, kindness, and respect...
descriptor_details.explanation: Work with students creating positive/supportive environment optimizing learning for all. Positive environment where all feel belong, welcome, trust, encouraged. Provide opportunities building social skills/strategies.

descriptor_details.descriptor: Teacher seeks out and is receptive to the interests and opinions of all students.
descriptor_details.explanation: First step differentiating for interests is finding out what students care/like. Provide opportunities connecting interests. Engagement deepens with connection. Connecting learning to real-world key technique.
possible_evidence: Teacher incorporates student opinions/ideas into lessons

descriptor_details.descriptor: Positive relationships and interdependence characterize the classroom.

Level_3_Proficient.description_header: Some Evidence of Student-Centered Learning/Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Teacher Establishes the Environment
descriptors: Teacher-student interactions are generally positive and reflect awareness and consideration of all students’ backgrounds.
Teacher and students exhibit respect and kindness for the teacher and each other; classroom is free of unhealthy conflict, sarcasm, and put-downs.
Teacher is receptive to the interests and opinions of students.

Level_1_Unsatisfactory.description_header: Minimal Evidence of Student Ownership of the Learning Environment – Heavy Emphasis on Teacher Direction
descriptors: Teacher does not establish a safe and positive classroom for students.
Students do not exhibit respect for the teacher or each other.
Teacher and/or student interaction and communication is characterized by unhealthy conflict, sarcasm, or put-downs.
Teacher is not receptive to interests and opinions of students.

suggested_coaching_questions: How do students respectfully challenge each other when they have differing views?
Why is it important to foster positive student-to-student interactions to promote care, kindness, and respect in the classroom?
Are students empowered to make decisions? How do you know?
Why is it important to know what students are interested in?
How does showing respect facilitate student interdependence?
In this lesson, how are students going to work together to extend each other’s thinking?

definitions.Expectations_Success_Criteria: Refers to a concrete learning performance: something students will say, do, or make to indicate they are moving toward the learning goal/objective.
definitions.High_quality_instructional_materials_HQI: Fully aligned to state content standards (or national/local if state not provided) - what students expected to learn/do end of grade/course - and builds content-specific knowledge/skills. Provides support for all learners and high-quality resources for teachers for meaningful instruction daily, including effective lesson structures/strategies, appropriate pacing guidance, meaningful connected assessments, implementation guidance/resources.

appendices_summary.Appendix_A_Other_Personnel: Provides specific observation guidance for Alternative School Educators, Special Education Educators (SWD), Interventionists, Librarian/Media Specialists (LMS), Master/Lead Teachers/Instructional Coaches.
appendices_summary.Appendix_C_Evaluation_Calculations: Details Bulletin 130 Effectiveness Ratings (5-point scale), Observation Requirements, Designated Observers, Component Weights (Qualitative 50%, Growth 50%), VAM info, SLT info, Certification criteria.
appendices_summary.Appendix_D_Pre_Conference: Guidance and template for pre-conference planning and execution.
appendices_summary.Appendix_E_Post_Conference: Guidance, template, scoring rubric, and report template for post-conference.
appendices_summary.Appendix_F_Coaching_Support: Guidance on Coaching Continuum, Follow-up Coaching/Support Plan Cycle, and PGP/Coaching Plan Template and Criteria.
